Cargo dependency manifest or download pinned to compromised onering 1.4.1 AIDelivery Medium
Catches the supply-chain ingress: file writes to Cargo.lock / Cargo.toml mentioning the malicious crate version, or HTTPS downloads of the onering 1.4.1 crate tarball from crates.io. Targets the build-time moment when a dev pulls the poisoned dependency, before build.rs runs. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit IOC `onering 1.4.1 from crates.io`. Cargo writes the cache file `onering-1.4.1.crate` under `~/.cargo/registry/cache/<index>/` and updates Cargo.lock with the pinned version on resolve — both are deterministic side-effects of pulling the poisoned dep. Article also flags that the GitHub repo is compromised, so we keep the file-write detection generic enough to fire on git-cloned dependencies (where the URL fetch wouldn't trigger). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/registries.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher or detection engineer intentionally fetching the IOC for sandboxing
  • Mirror/proxy of crates.io pre-fetching the malicious version into local cache before a yank propagates
  • Vulnerability scanner like cargo-audit or Aikido enumerating the version
  • Legacy CI pipeline still referencing onering 1.4.1 after yank but on an isolated build agent
  • Developer cleaning up `Cargo.lock` after a known-bad pull (Cargo writes the file even on `cargo update --precise` to a safe version, with onering removed)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the host's `~/.cargo/registry/cache/**/onering-1.4.1.crate` and confirm SHA256 matches the malicious tarball; grep every repo on disk for `onering` in Cargo.lock and note the version. 2) Contain: instruct the dev to `cargo update -p onering --precise <safe-version>` or remove the dependency, force a fresh `cargo build` in a clean target dir, and on shared CI invalidate the cargo cache. 3) Hunt: across the org's source-control, run `git grep -E 'onering.*=.*"1\.4\.1"'` on every Rust repo; check internal Cargo mirrors for any hosts that pulled the bad version; coordinate with Aikido feed for org-wide blast radius.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "crates.io" and (RemoteUrl has "onering/1.4.1" or RemoteUrl has "onering-1.4.1.crate")
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where FileName in~ ("Cargo.lock", "Cargo.toml")
 | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe", "cargo")
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where FolderPath has ".cargo\\registry\\cache" or FolderPath has ".cargo/registry/cache"
 | where FileName has "onering-1.4.1"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Url has "crates.io" and (Url has "onering/1.4.1" or Url has "onering-1.4.1.crate")
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod),
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where TargetFileName in~ ("Cargo.lock", "Cargo.toml")
 | where ActingProcessName has "cargo"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where TargetFileName has "onering-1.4.1"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:zeek (@http.url:*crates.io*onering\/1.4.1* OR @http.url:*crates.io*onering-1.4.1.crate*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:*\/.cargo\/registry\/cache\/*onering-1.4.1*) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*\\.cargo\\registry\\cache\\*onering-1.4.1* OR @TargetFilename:*\\Cargo.lock OR @TargetFilename:*\\Cargo.toml))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten (TargetFileName=/onering-1\.4\.1/i OR (TargetFileName=/[\\/](Cargo\.lock|Cargo\.toml)$/i ContextImageFileName=/cargo(\.exe)?$/i))) OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(static\.)?crates\.io/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Unpatched June 2026 Patch Tuesday CVE inventory (kernel TCP/IP, DHCP, HTTP.sys, BitLocker)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] DHCP Client svchost anomalous child process (CVE-2026-44815 post-exploit) · [LLM] HTTP.sys / IIS w3wp.exe spawning shell or LOLBin (CVE-2026-47291 post-exploit) · [LLM] CTFMON spawning elevated child or CTFMON-hosted privilege escalation (CVE-2026-45586 / GreenPlasma) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft Patches Record 206 Flaws, Including Three Zero-Days and Critical RCE B
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PoC artefact drop — Chaotic Eclipse named exploits (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, RoguePlanet, bitskrieg)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] HTTP/2 Bomb mitigation tampering — MaxHeadersCount registry value (CVE-2026-49160) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Unpatched June 2026 Patch Tuesday CVE inventory (kernel TCP/IP, DHCP, HTTP.sys, BitLocker) AIWeaponization High
Surface hosts in the org still missing the June 2026 Patch Tuesday updates for the critical pre-auth RCEs (CVE-2026-45657 kernel TCP/IP, CVE-2026-47291 HTTP.sys, CVE-2026-44815 DHCP Client) and the publicly-disclosed zero-days (CVE-2026-45586 CTFMON, CVE-2026-49160 HTTP.sys DoS, CVE-2026-50507 BitLocker). Use Defender TVM software vulnerability data — these CVEs are all in the June 2026 KB rollup and require none of the others to be exploitable. Rationale: Uses the exact CVE list pulled out of the article body (CVE-2026-45657/47291/44815/45585/45655/45658/50507/45586/49160 plus the two non-Microsoft CVE-2025-10263 and CVE-2026-8863). TVM joins keep it to vulnerable software actually installed, not just the CVE catalogue.
ATT&CKT1190 T1588.006
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Devices in active patching maintenance windows scheduled within 24-48h
  • Air-gapped lab/test hosts on intentional patch holds
  • Servers in change-freeze where TVM hasn't re-scanned post-patch yet
  • DCs requiring staged kernel-driver reboots (CVE-2026-45657 is the kernel TCP/IP fix)
  • Hosts where MDE sensor health is degraded and inventory is stale
Suppression filter
| where VulnerabilitySeverityLevel in~ ("Critical","High")
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — sort by `ExposedDevices` desc, then by `IsExploitAvailable=true` per CveId; surface CVE-2026-45657/47291/44815 first since they are unauthenticated network RCEs. Step 2: Contain — for any internet-facing host (check DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing) missing CVE-2026-47291 or -44815, push emergency KB via Intune/SCCM and consider firewalling 80/443/UDP67-68 from untrusted networks until patched. Step 3: Hunt — pivot on the still-exposed devices into the other UCs in this set (HTTP.sys/DHCP child-process anomalies, MaxHeadersCount registry tampering, CTFMON LPE) to confirm none have already been exploited pre-patch.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45585","CVE-2026-45655","CVE-2026-45658","CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-45586","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-8863","CVE-2025-10263")
| join kind=leftouter DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB on CveId
| summarize ExposedDevices = dcount(DeviceId),
            SampleDevices  = make_set(DeviceName, 25),
            FirstSeen      = min(Timestamp),
            MaxCvss        = max(CvssScore),
            ExploitAvailable = max(tostring(IsExploitAvailable))
            by CveId, SoftwareName, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel
| order by MaxCvss desc, ExposedDevices desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45585","CVE-2026-45655","CVE-2026-45658","CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-45586","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-8863","CVE-2025-10263")
| summarize ExposedDevices = dcount(DeviceId),
            SampleDevices  = make_set(DeviceName, 25),
            FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
            MaxSeverity    = max(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel)
            by CveId, SoftwareName, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45585","CVE-2026-45655","CVE-2026-45658","CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-45586","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-8863","CVE-2025-10263") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.signature | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | sort 0 - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45585","CVE-2026-45655","CVE-2026-45658","CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-45586","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-8863","CVE-2025-10263") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.signature | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | sort 0 - severity
HTTP/2 Bomb mitigation tampering — MaxHeadersCount registry value (CVE-2026-49160) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Watch for write, delete, or downward modification of the new `MaxHeadersCount` registry value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters. Microsoft introduced this value specifically to mitigate the HTTP/2 Bomb DoS against IIS/HTTP.sys (CVE-2026-49160). An attacker who reaches admin on an IIS host could remove or set it to 0 to re-enable the DoS surface; conversely the value going from set→unset on a host that previously had it is a tampering signal. Rationale: Pulls the exact registry path and value name (`MaxHeadersCount` under `HTTP\Parameters`) that the article quotes Microsoft as introducing in the June 2026 update. Tamper-with-the-mitigation is a higher-fidelity signal than trying to detect the HTTP/2 Bomb payload itself on the wire, which IIS logs don't expose at header-count granularity.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin manually applying or tuning the new mitigation (legitimate IIS hardening sweep)
  • Configuration management tools (DSC / Ansible / GPO) deploying the registry value across an IIS fleet
  • Microsoft KB rollback during a problematic patch cycle
  • IIS performance team raising the limit above default for a high-header app
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MsiExec.exe","services.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — pull `InitiatingProcessFileName` and account; legitimate sets come from `services.exe`/`TrustedInstaller.exe` or known CM agents. Anything signed by an interactive user, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or LOLBins is suspicious. Step 2: Contain — if change is unexpected, restore the value (>= 100 is Microsoft's default, see KB) and snapshot the IIS host. Step 3: Hunt — look back 24h on the same host for w3wp.exe spawning shells, IIS module installs (`appcmd.exe install module`), or unexpected HTTP/2 traffic spikes; pivot to the HTTP.sys/IIS anomalous-child UC.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "MaxHeadersCount"
| where ActionType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryValueDeleted","RegistryKeyDeleted")
| extend NewVal = tostring(RegistryValueData), PrevVal = tostring(PreviousRegistryValueData)
| where ActionType != "RegistryValueSet" or NewVal in ("0","0x0","") or toint(NewVal) < toint(coalesce(PrevVal,"0"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, NewVal, PrevVal,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters"
| where RegistryValue =~ "MaxHeadersCount"
| where EventType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryValueDeleted","RegistryKeyDeleted")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData,
          RegistryPreviousValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HTTP.sys MaxHeadersCount Mitigation Tampering (CVE-2026-49160 HTTP/2 Bomb)
id: 8d1f3a72-2a2f-4b91-9e6b-f1b3d2e4a0c7
description: Detects modification or deletion of the MaxHeadersCount registry value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters, which Microsoft introduced in the June 2026 patch as the mitigation for the HTTP/2 Bomb DoS (CVE-2026-49160). Removal or zeroing of this value re-enables the DoS surface against IIS / HTTP.sys.

DHCP Client svchost anomalous child process (CVE-2026-44815 post-exploit) AIExploitation High
CVE-2026-44815 is a pre-auth stack-overflow RCE in the Windows DHCP Client. The DHCP Client service runs in svchost.exe under the `LocalServiceNetworkRestricted` host with the `Dhcp` service argument. Successful exploitation would surface as svchost (DHCP-hosted) spawning a non-svchost child — there is essentially no legitimate reason for `Dhcp`-hosted svchost to create a shell, script host, or LOLBin. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-44815 ... allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network ... systems handling DHCP traffic should be treated as high-priority patch targets.' DHCP Client svchost normally never spawns shells; pairing the parent (`-s Dhcp` / `LocalServiceNetworkRestricted`) with the LocalService SID and a LOLBin child is a low-FP combination.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Microsoft DHCP troubleshooting kits running `ipconfig.exe` under the service context
  • Endpoint management agents (Intune/SCCM) invoking `net.exe` via the DHCP host briefly during network re-init
  • MDM remediation scripts that target DHCP renewal
  • Sysinternals procdump / handle.exe by IR team taking dumps of svchost
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !has "ipconfig /renew"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — confirm the parent command line really contains `-s Dhcp` (not another svchost service); pull the SHA256 of the child and the network connections from the same `InitiatingProcessId` ±5 min. Step 2: Contain — isolate the host with Defender 'Isolate device' or NAC quarantine; capture the DHCP packet trace if still online (rogue DHCP server may be persistent on the LAN). Step 3: Hunt — across the same subnet, look for additional DHCP Client hosts that received a DHCP OFFER from the same MAC, and pivot to the patch-inventory UC for CVE-2026-44815 to find other still-vulnerable hosts on the same broadcast domain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "svchost.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-s Dhcp", "-s dhcp", "LocalServiceNetworkRestricted")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe","hostname.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage=FolderPath,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\svchost.exe"
| extend NewBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewBase in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe")
| where SubjectUserSid in ("S-1-5-19","S-1-5-20")  // LOCAL SERVICE / NETWORK SERVICE — DHCP runs as LocalService
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, ProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HTTP.sys / IIS w3wp.exe spawning shell or LOLBin (CVE-2026-47291 post-exploit) AIExploitation High
CVE-2026-47291 is an integer overflow in HTTP.sys (kernel) allowing unauthenticated network RCE. Post-exploitation in IIS environments typically surfaces as the w3wp.exe app-pool worker spawning cmd/powershell or LOLBins, or as `System` process anomalies. This rule pivots on the w3wp parent → suspicious child shape which is essentially absent in healthy IIS operations. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-47291 ... integer overflow ... in Windows HTTP.sys that allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.' HTTP.sys is a kernel driver, but IIS deployments funnel HTTP.sys traffic into w3wp.exe app-pool workers — successful exploitation gives the attacker code in that context. w3wp spawning cmd/PowerShell is high-fidelity (legitimate web apps rarely shell out).
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy ASP.NET apps using `Process.Start("cmd /c ...")` for legitimate batch work (e.g. PDF rendering, ImageMagick wrappers)
  • SharePoint or Exchange Health Manager scripts that invoke PowerShell from w3wp
  • WebDeploy / msdeploy.exe operations during application deploys
  • Web-based admin consoles (HelpDesk apps, ITSM portals) that legitimately invoke `net.exe`/`whoami.exe` on behalf of authenticated admins
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !contains "WebDeploy" and ChildCmd !contains "msdeploy"
| where ParentCmd !contains "HealthMailbox"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — pull the parent w3wp.exe command line to identify the IIS App Pool (`-ap` argument). Check if that pool is on a known-legacy/known-shells allowlist for the org; if not, treat as live. Step 2: Contain — recycle the App Pool, capture a memory dump of w3wp.exe via Sysinternals procdump, and isolate the host. Pull the IIS access logs for the 5 minutes prior — large or malformed POSTs to .aspx/.asmx handlers are the likely vector. Step 3: Hunt — search the IIS inetpub wwwroot folders for new .aspx/.ashx/.config files created by the IIS worker (web shells), and pivot to CVE-2026-47291 patch status across the IIS fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","ipconfig.exe","hostname.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentIntegrity=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ChildImage=FolderPath,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildIntegrity=ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\w3wp.exe"
| extend NewBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewBase in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","ipconfig.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CTFMON spawning elevated child or CTFMON-hosted privilege escalation (CVE-2026-45586 / GreenPlasma) AIExploitation Medium
CVE-2026-45586 is a privilege-escalation flaw in the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON), publicly disclosed as a zero-day and suspected to be the GreenPlasma PoC released by Chaotic Eclipse. CTFMON normally only spawns IME/language helpers at the user's own integrity level. Detection: ctfmon.exe (or its CTF API consumers) spawning a child at High/System integrity, or an integrity-level escalation event whose initiating process is ctfmon.exe. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-45586 ... Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON) privilege escalation' and 'suspected to be a fix for a zero-day privilege escalation exploit that Chaotic Eclipse released under the name GreenPlasma.' ctfmon.exe legitimately spawns only language-bar helpers at the user's own integrity. A high-integrity child from a medium-integrity parent is a textbook LPE signal.
ATT&CKT1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Error Reporting auto-launching wermgr.exe/WerFault.exe under ctfmon — filtered above
  • MUI / language pack installer running under TrustedInstaller (parent would already be High integrity — caught by the integrity-delta filter)
  • Sysinternals AccessChk by an IR team checking CTF token integrity
  • RDP language input service restart during a console handoff
Suppression filter
| where ChildImage !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
| where ParentImage !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — confirm the integrity delta (parent Medium / child High or System). Pull the SHA256 of the spawned child binary and any registry writes by ctfmon ±60s (CTFMON COM hijack patterns write to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\CTF). Step 2: Contain — kill the elevated child, isolate the host, capture a memory dump of ctfmon.exe and the elevated child. Step 3: Hunt — back-search 30 days for the same SHA256 anywhere in the fleet (likely PoC artefact named after GreenPlasma/MiniPlasma), and pivot to the CVE-2026-45586 patch-status UC to find unpatched hosts that could be next.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "ctfmon.exe"
| where FileName !in~ ("ctfmon.exe","conhost.exe","wermgr.exe","WerFault.exe")
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("High","System")
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel !in~ ("High","System")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentIntegrity=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage=FolderPath,
          ChildIntegrity=ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\ctfmon.exe"
| extend NewBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewBase !in ("ctfmon.exe","conhost.exe","wermgr.exe","werfault.exe")
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936","%%1937")  // Full Token (admin) — the LPE outcome
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CTFMON Spawning Elevated Child (CVE-2026-45586 GreenPlasma LPE)
id: 7a1e4c83-6f2b-4a93-b5c1-d4e8f1a02c3d
description: Detects ctfmon.exe (Collaborative Translation Framework) spawning a child process at High or System integrity from a non-elevated parent context. Consistent with exploitation of CVE-2026-45586 — the CTFMON privilege-escalation zero-day publicly disclosed by Chaotic Eclipse as 'GreenPlasma' before the June 2026 patch.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-patches-record-206-flaws.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\ctfmon.exe'
    IntegrityLevel:
      - 'High'
      - 'System'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ctfmon.exe'
      - '\conhost.exe'
      - '\wermgr.exe'
      - '\WerFault.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\ctfmon.exe OR *\\Ctfmon.exe OR *\\CTFMON.EXE)) (@IntegrityLevel:(High OR System)) -@Image:(*\\ctfmon.exe OR *\\Ctfmon.exe OR *\\conhost.exe OR *\\WerFault.exe OR *\\wermgr.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/ctfmon\.exe$/i
| IntegrityLevel=/^(High|System)$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(ctfmon|conhost|wermgr|WerFault)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName, IntegrityLevel], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as child_integrity values(Processes.parent_process_integrity_level) as parent_integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="ctfmon.exe" Processes.process_integrity_level IN ("high","system") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where parent_integrity!="high" AND parent_integrity!="system"
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as child_integrity values(Processes.parent_process_integrity_level) as parent_integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="ctfmon.exe" Processes.process_integrity_level IN ("high","system") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where parent_integrity!="high" AND parent_integrity!="system"
PoC artefact drop — Chaotic Eclipse named exploits (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, RoguePlanet, bitskrieg) AIInstallation Low
Article references five publicly-released PoCs by researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse): YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585 BitLocker bypass), GreenPlasma (CVE-2026-45586 CTFMON LPE), MiniPlasma (CVE-2020-17103 print spooler incomplete fix), RoguePlanet (Microsoft Defender race-condition to SYSTEM cmd), and bitskrieg (CVE-2026-50507 BitLocker full-data bypass). Hunt for file writes or process executions whose name or folder contains these PoC code-names — researchers and red-teamers commonly preserve the published name in repo/binary names, and uplifted commodity attackers often do not bother to rename. Rationale: Article explicitly names the five Chaotic Eclipse / Nightmare-Eclipse PoCs (YellowKey for CVE-2026-45585, GreenPlasma for CVE-2026-45586, MiniPlasma against CVE-2020-17103, RoguePlanet for the Defender race condition, bitskrieg for CVE-2026-50507). String-name hunting is low-precision but high-recall; useful for catching unsophisticated reuse of the public PoCs before defenders patch.
ATT&CKT1588.005 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red team / pentest engagement legitimately downloading the PoCs to a test host
  • Security researchers in the org investigating the PoCs in a sandbox VM
  • Threat intel team archiving copies for analysis
  • Documentation / blog posts (.html, .pdf) referencing the names — high FP on browser cache hits
  • Wallpaper or theme files coincidentally named (yellow key, etc.)
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Cache\"
| where FolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cache\"
| where FileName !endswith ".pdf" and FileName !endswith ".html" and FileName !endswith ".htm"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — distinguish PoC binaries (.exe, .ps1, .py, .dll) from documentation files (.pdf, .html, .docx). For binary hits, pull SHA256 and check it against VirusTotal / internal sandbox. For doc hits, check user role (red team / IR / researcher allowlist). Step 2: Contain — if a binary executed on a non-research host, isolate and capture memory + the binary. Confirm whether the corresponding CVE patch was applied; if not, the host may already be compromised at the privilege level the PoC achieves (SYSTEM for RoguePlanet/GreenPlasma, encrypted-data access for YellowKey/bitskrieg). Step 3: Hunt — pull the InitiatingProcessAccountName and look 24h back/forward for that user's other activity (downloads, browser, USB). Pivot to the patch-status UC for the matching CVE.
let Codenames = dynamic(["yellowkey","greenplasma","miniplasma","rogueplanet","bitskrieg"]);
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
    | extend low_name = tolower(FileName), low_path = tolower(FolderPath)
    | where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_path has_any (Codenames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | extend low_cmd = tolower(ProcessCommandLine), low_img = tolower(FolderPath), low_name = tolower(FileName)
    | where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_img has_any (Codenames) or low_cmd has_any (Codenames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let Codenames = dynamic(["yellowkey","greenplasma","miniplasma","rogueplanet","bitskrieg"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| extend low_path = tolower(TargetFilePath), low_name = tolower(TargetFileName)
| where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_path has_any (Codenames)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn

// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable phpBB instances (≤3.3.16 / 4.0.0-a2) exposing CVE-2026-29199 · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)

Vulnerable phpBB instances (≤3.3.16 / 4.0.0-a2) exposing CVE-2026-29199 AIReconnaissance High
Inventory-based hunt that surfaces phpBB installs running versions vulnerable to the unauthenticated session-takeover bug disclosed by Aikido. Used to prioritise patching to 3.3.17 before mass exploitation begins now that the advisory is public. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit version cut-off (3.3.16 and 4.0.0-a2 vulnerable, 3.3.17 fixed) and the CVE assignment. TVM-based asset hunt is the right shape for a zero-day-no-IOCs disclosure — patch-state visibility now, behavioural detection once technical details land. Cross-checked against the Aikido blog and the phpBB 3.3.17 release notes referenced in the post. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Development/staging phpBB instances intentionally pinned to an old version for compatibility testing
  • Vulnerability scanner banner-grab misidentifies a phpBB fork (e.g. phpBB-CMS bridge) with its own version scheme
  • TVM reports the bundled phpBB version inside a third-party hosting control panel (Plesk/cPanel) where the host vendor patches separately
  • Honeypot or research phpBB deliberately left unpatched
  • Internet-Archive style read-only mirror of an old forum
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("-dev","-staging","-test","honeypot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm asset is internet-exposed (check public DNS, perimeter ACLs); pull the phpBB config.php to verify the live running version vs. TVM-reported. 2) Contain: if exposed and unpatched, take the forum off-line or place behind WAF rule blocking POST to /ucp.php?mode=login_external and any /user/oauth/* paths until upgraded; force-rotate the admin password and the forum_admin/forum_mod session secrets after patching. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (anomalous OAuth endpoint sessions) and UC3 (PHP writes by web-server process) across the last 14 days for any sign of prior exploitation; check phpBB's admin log table for unfamiliar admin sessions or template edits.

Unauthenticated session creation burst against phpBB OAuth/login endpoints AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the public-facing web logs for a single source IP that receives multiple distinct phpBB session cookies (phpbb3_*_sid) on unauthenticated requests to login / OAuth callback endpoints — the observable shape of mass account takeover via the CVE-2026-29199 single-request bypass. Rationale: The article confirms (a) a single unauthenticated request returns a valid session as any chosen user and (b) the default-public member list makes target selection trivial — at scale, the observable on the web tier is one source IP harvesting many sessions in a short window against ucp.php / /user/oauth/. The patched safe path /user/oauth/authenticate/... is explicitly named in the post and bracketing it covers both old and new endpoint variants. Defender Advanced Hunting has no public-web access log table so defender_kql intentionally empty. Datadog/Falcon left empty — pipeline doesn't have a confirmed phpBB web-log source path. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate SSO/OAuth bursts after maintenance window where many users re-authenticate at once
  • Web crawler or uptime monitor that issues unauthenticated GETs to /ucp.php and gets a guest session cookie each time
  • Load tester / synthetic transaction monitor probing login flow
  • Forum migration tool re-importing user accounts via login_external path
  • Aggressive caching CDN that strips Cookie headers, causing the origin to mint a new session per hit
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("<load-balancer-internal-ip>", "<monitoring-egress-ip>") and csUserAgent !has_any ("Pingdom", "UptimeRobot", "StatusCake", "Site24x7")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull all session cookies issued to the offending IP; in phpBB DB, look up phpbb_sessions.session_user_id values bound to those SIDs — if multiple distinct, non-anonymous (user_id != 1) user_ids appear, this is exploitation, not noise. 2) Contain: invalidate every session row for the affected user_ids, force password reset for those accounts (especially anyone in the founder/admin groups), and block the source IP at WAF/perimeter; if 3.3.17 not yet applied, take the forum offline immediately. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC3 for webshell drop, search phpBB_log table for admin actions from those sessions, and check for any new entries in phpbb_styles / phpbb_extensions written within the same window.
let SuspectPaths = dynamic(["/ucp.php","/user/oauth/","/user/oauth/authenticate/"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has_any (SuspectPaths) or csUriQuery has_any ("mode=login", "login=external", "oauth_service")
| where scStatus in (200, 302)
| summarize Hits = count(), DistinctUriCombos = dcount(strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery)), DistinctUAs = dcount(csUserAgent), SamplePaths = make_set(csUriStem, 10), SampleQueries = make_set(csUriQuery, 10) by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where Hits >= 20 and DistinctUriCombos >= 5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Web.cookie) as session_cookie_count values(Web.uri_path) as paths values(Web.user) as observed_users min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php*" OR Web.url="*/user/oauth/*" OR Web.uri_path="*ucp.php*" OR Web.uri_path="*/user/oauth/*") AND Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where session_cookie_count >= 5 | eval reason="5+ distinct phpBB session cookies issued to single source IP touching login/OAuth path — review for CVE-2026-29199 mass takeover" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Web.cookie) as session_cookie_count values(Web.uri_path) as paths values(Web.user) as observed_users min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php*" OR Web.url="*/user/oauth/*" OR Web.uri_path="*ucp.php*" OR Web.uri_path="*/user/oauth/*") AND Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where session_cookie_count >= 5 | eval reason="5+ distinct phpBB session cookies issued to single source IP touching login/OAuth path — review for CVE-2026-29199 mass takeover" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Web-server process writing PHP under phpBB content directories (post-RCE webshell drop) AIInstallation Medium
Detects the standard phpBB ACP-to-RCE follow-on after admin takeover via CVE-2026-29199: the web-server process (w3wp.exe / php-fpm / httpd / nginx) writing a new .php file into phpBB writable directories (/cache/, /store/, /files/, /images/avatars/upload/, /ext/, /styles/). phpBB's RCE primitive on admin accounts has historically been template/style/extension editing, all of which land here. Rationale: The article explicitly states admin compromise via CVE-2026-29199 'opens the door to Remote Code Execution.' phpBB's well-known RCE primitive after ACP access is editing a style/template or installing a malicious extension — both write PHP into the dirs anchored above. Web-server-process-as-parent + new .php in writable phpBB dir is a high-fidelity composite (parent + child + path) per the KQL house-style anti-bare-process-execution rule. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB upgrade (3.3.16 → 3.3.17) writing new core/extension .php files under /ext/ and /styles/
  • Administrator legitimately installing a third-party extension via Customise → Manage extensions
  • phpBB cache rebuild writing compiled Twig output under /cache/twig/ (compiled PHP)
  • Composer dependency install during a phpBB extension deploy
  • Backup/restore tool unpacking phpBB tarball back into the document root
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","phpbb_install","adm/index.php?i=acp_extensions") or TargetFilePath has "/cache/twig/")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the new .php and search VirusTotal / your malware reputation feed; cat the first 256 bytes — a webshell almost always starts with <?php and contains eval/assert/system/passthru/base64_decode. Check phpBB phpbb_log for admin actions immediately preceding the file write. 2) Contain: take the affected phpBB document root offline behind a maintenance page; remove the dropped file; rotate ALL admin passwords and the config.php DB password; revoke any new user_ids elevated to admin group during the suspect window. 3) Hunt: across all phpBB hosts, run the same query for the past 14 days; check for additional persistence (cron entries, modified .htaccess, new entries in phpbb_extensions table); pivot to UC2 to find the source IP that drove the initial session takeover.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\cache\", @"/cache/", @"\store\", @"/store/", @"\files\", @"/files/", @"\images\avatars\upload\", @"/images/avatars/upload/", @"\ext\", @"/ext/", @"\styles\", @"/styles/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/cache/", "/store/", "/files/", "/images/avatars/upload/", "/ext/", "/styles/", "\\cache\\", "\\store\\", "\\files\\", "\\ext\\", "\\styles\\")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("w3wp.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "php-fpm", "httpd", "apache2", "nginx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access on Updated Windows

The Hacker News
2026-06-10 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The anonymous security researcher going by the name Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse) has released a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for yet another Microsoft Defender zero-day named RoguePlanet. "The exploit is a race condition, so it's a hit or miss," the researcher, who published the exploit under a new GitHub account "MSNightmare" said. "I have managed to get a 100% success rate on

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] DNS / network connection to RoguePlanet PoC publication domain (projectnightcrawler.dev) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Microsoft Defender service spawning interactive shell as SYSTEM (RoguePlanet exploit success signature) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
DNS / network connection to RoguePlanet PoC publication domain (projectnightcrawler.dev) AIDelivery High
Hunts for any host in the estate resolving or connecting to projectnightcrawler.dev, the publication channel associated with Chaotic Eclipse / MSNightmare's RoguePlanet Defender LPE PoC. First-touch on this domain in an enterprise environment is almost certainly a curious admin or an attacker staging the PoC rather than legitimate business traffic. Rationale: projectnightcrawler.dev is the pre-extracted IOC tied to the Chaotic Eclipse / Nightmare-Eclipse publishing infrastructure for the RoguePlanet PoC. Any internal host reaching this domain is either a curious admin pulling the PoC for testing or — given that the prior three Defender flaws (BlueHammer/UnDefend/RedSun) were exploited in the wild post-disclosure — an attacker staging the LPE. First-touch is high-fidelity because the domain has no legitimate enterprise use. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1588/005/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/
ATT&CKT1588.005 T1071.004 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red team or internal vulnerability researcher pulling the PoC to test exposure of patched endpoints
  • Threat-intel analyst accessing the Blogger / GitHub mirror from a SOC workstation
  • Security vendor sandbox detonating malware samples that reference the URL
  • Curious admin reading the THN article and clicking through to the source
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("redteam-svc", "vuln-researcher") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sandboxie.exe", "cuckoo.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user/process initiating the connection — pivot on InitiatingProcessFileName/CommandLine in DeviceNetworkEvents. If it's a browser launched by an IT/security user, validate with the user. 2) Contain: block the domain at the proxy/firewall, isolate the device if a non-browser process (powershell.exe, curl.exe, MsMpEng-spawned shells) initiated the connection, and grab the parent process tree. 3) Hunt: pivot to DeviceProcessEvents on the same host for new SYSTEM-context children of MsMpEng.exe or MpDefenderCoreService.exe (RoguePlanet success signature), check DeviceFileEvents for downloaded .iso / PoC executables, and review the device for the prior Chaotic Eclipse CVEs CVE-2026-33825, CVE-2026-45498, CVE-2026-41091 — patch status and any earlier exploitation IOCs.

  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

  | where RemoteUrl has SuspiciousDomain or AdditionalFields has SuspiciousDomain
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields),
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileOriginUrl has SuspiciousDomain or FileOriginReferrerUrl has SuspiciousDomain
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc

  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),

title: Network or DNS Activity to RoguePlanet Defender Zero-Day PoC Domain
id: 5b2d6f8c-1a9e-4f2b-83d7-7a3e0c4f9d11
description: Detects DNS or HTTP activity to projectnightcrawler.dev, the publication channel for Chaotic Eclipse / MSNightmare's RoguePlanet Microsoft Defender zero-day PoC granting SYSTEM privileges on patched Windows 10/11.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-defender-rogueplanet-zero-day.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1588.005
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains: 'projectnightcrawler.dev'
  condition: selection
level: high
(source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender OR cisco.firepower OR zscaler) AND (@DestinationHostname:*projectnightcrawler.dev* OR @QueryName:*projectnightcrawler.dev* OR @dns.question.name:*projectnightcrawler.dev* OR @http.url:*projectnightcrawler.dev* OR @network.destination.domain:*projectnightcrawler.dev*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)projectnightcrawler\.dev$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=/^NetworkConnect/ RemoteAddressIP4=*)
| case { #event_simpleName=DnsRequest | * } | * 
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
| sort(count, order=desc)
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.answer) as answers values(DNS.src) as src_hosts from datamodel=Network_Resolution where (DNS.query="projectnightcrawler.dev" OR DNS.query="*.projectnightcrawler.dev") by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*projectnightcrawler.dev*" OR Web.site="projectnightcrawler.dev") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.answer) as answers values(DNS.src) as src_hosts from datamodel=Network_Resolution where (DNS.query="projectnightcrawler.dev" OR DNS.query="*.projectnightcrawler.dev") by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*projectnightcrawler.dev*" OR Web.site="projectnightcrawler.dev") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Microsoft Defender service spawning interactive shell as SYSTEM (RoguePlanet exploit success signature) AIExploitation High
Hunts for the post-exploitation signature of a successful RoguePlanet (or BlueHammer/UnDefend/RedSun) Defender LPE: the Defender service process (MsMpEng.exe, MpDefenderCoreService.exe, NisSrv.exe, MpCmdRun.exe) spawning a child cmd.exe / powershell.exe / conhost.exe running in SYSTEM integrity. Defender service should never legitimately launch an interactive shell — when it does, treat it as a confirmed-exploited host. Rationale: The article states that successful RoguePlanet exploitation yields 'a shell with SYSTEM-level privileges' via the Defender process. Because Defender's antimalware service (MsMpEng.exe / MpDefenderCoreService.exe / NisSrv.exe) already runs as SYSTEM, the natural exploitation primitive is to have it spawn the attacker's shell — that parent-child relationship is the high-fidelity signature, and it covers the prior in-the-wild-exploited Chaotic Eclipse flaws (CVE-2026-33825, CVE-2026-45498, CVE-2026-41091) as well. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1211/
ATT&CKT1068 T1211 T1059.003 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MpCmdRun.exe spawning conhost.exe during scheduled signature update or full scan (legitimate, runs in SYSTEM)
  • Endpoint engineer running MpCmdRun.exe -Scan manually from an elevated shell that re-parents under MpCmdRun
  • Defender Platform Update orchestrator launching cmd.exe to invoke a config script during definition install
  • SecurityHealthService.exe spawning rundll32 to load a notification helper DLL during user-context UI events
  • Third-party EDR using PsExec-like service injection that imitates this parent-child shape
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and FileName =~ "conhost.exe" and isempty(ProcessCommandLine)) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "SecurityHealthService.exe" and FileName =~ "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "SecurityHealthSSO")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full process tree (parent of MsMpEng.exe, the spawned shell, any grandchildren) and the SHA256 of all three. Validate token: a real Defender update spawns conhost briefly with no follow-on activity; an exploit spawns cmd/powershell that survives and emits child processes (whoami, net, reg, msiexec). 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender LiveResponse or network containment, kill the shell and its descendants, snapshot memory before reboot. 3) Hunt: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents from the same DeviceId for projectnightcrawler.dev contact within the prior 24h, search DeviceFileEvents for .iso mounts immediately preceding the shell (the PoC requires standard-user ISO mount), and across the estate query DeviceProcessEvents for any host where Defender process spawned a non-conhost child in SYSTEM context — a single broader hunt to catch unknown variants.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe", "MpDefenderCoreService.exe", "NisSrv.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe", "SecurityHealthService.exe", "MsSense.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "conhost.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "rundll32.exe")
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in ("System", "High") or AccountSid == "S-1-5-18" or AccountName =~ "system"
| extend ParentDir = tostring(split(InitiatingProcessFolderPath, "\\")[-2])
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, AccountSid, ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\MsMpEng.exe", "\\MpDefenderCoreService.exe", "\\NisSrv.exe", "\\MpCmdRun.exe", "\\SecurityHealthService.exe", "\\MsSense.exe")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe", "\\powershell.exe", "\\pwsh.exe", "\\conhost.exe", "\\wscript.exe", "\\cscript.exe", "\\rundll32.exe")
  | where SubjectUserSid == "S-1-5-18" or TargetUserSid == "S-1-5-18" or TokenElevationType has "1936"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, TargetUserSid, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, EventID),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("MsMpEng.exe", "MpDefenderCoreService.exe", "NisSrv.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe", "SecurityHealthService.exe")
  | where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "conhost.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "rundll32.exe")
  | where TargetProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("System", "High")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessIntegrityLevel, EventVendor)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Defender Service Process Spawning Interactive Shell (RoguePlanet / CVE-2026-33825 / CVE-2026-45498 / CVE-2026-41091 LPE Signature)
id: 7c9f3a21-8d4b-4e6a-9f8c-2b5d7e0a1c3f
description: Detects MsMpEng.exe, MpDefenderCoreService.exe, NisSrv.exe, MpCmdRun.exe or SecurityHealthService.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, conhost.exe, wscript.exe or cscript.exe — the post-exploitation signature of Chaotic Eclipse's RoguePlanet zero-day and the related BlueHammer / UnDefend / RedSun Defender LPE chain that yields a SYSTEM-level shell.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-defender-rogueplanet-zero-day.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1211
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\MpDefenderCoreService.exe'
      - '\NisSrv.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
      - '\SecurityHealthService.exe'
      - '\MsSense.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\conhost.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Defender platform updates (MpCmdRun.exe legitimately spawning helper conhost during signature install)
  - Endpoint engineers running manual MpCmdRun.exe scans interactively
level: critical
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR windows.defender) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @ParentImage:(*\\MsMpEng.exe OR *\\msmpeng.exe OR *\\MpDefenderCoreService.exe OR *\\mpdefendercoreservice.exe OR *\\NisSrv.exe OR *\\nissrv.exe OR *\\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\\mpcmdrun.exe OR *\\SecurityHealthService.exe OR *\\securityhealthservice.exe OR *\\MsSense.exe OR *\\mssense.exe) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\conhost.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(msmpeng|mpdefendercoreservice|nissrv|mpcmdrun|securityhealthservice|mssense)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|conhost|wscript|cscript|rundll32)\.exe$/i
| IntegrityLevel="System" OR UserSid="S-1-5-18" OR UserName=/system$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName, IntegrityLevel], function=count())
| sort(count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.user) as users from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("MsMpEng.exe", "MpDefenderCoreService.exe", "NisSrv.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe", "SecurityHealthService.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "conhost.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.user Processes.process_integrity_level | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where (user="SYSTEM" OR user="NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM" OR process_integrity_level="System") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.user) as users from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("MsMpEng.exe", "MpDefenderCoreService.exe", "NisSrv.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe", "SecurityHealthService.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "conhost.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.user Processes.process_integrity_level | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where (user="SYSTEM" OR user="NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM" OR process_integrity_level="System") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-41091")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-41091")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:

detection:
