| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-39987", "CVE-2026-31431", "CVE-2026-43284", "CVE-2026-43500", "CVE-2024-21182", "CVE-2026-0257", "CVE-2026-45659")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-39987", "CVE-2026-31431", "CVE-2026-43284", "CVE-2026-43500", "CVE-2024-21182", "CVE-2026-0257", "CVE-2026-45659")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

New FROST Attack Lets Websites Track What Sites and Apps You Open via SSD Timing

The Hacker News
2026-06-09 7 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A malicious website can work out which sites you visit and which apps you open, using nothing but JavaScript and the timing of your SSD. The attack, called FROST, needs no native code, no extension, and no permission prompt. You open the page, leave the tab sitting there, and it watches the drive for contention in the background. Researchers at Graz University of Technology built it and

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children

Browser writing oversized OPFS file (potential FROST SSD-timing side-channel) AIReconnaissance Low
Hunts for a browser process (Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari) writing a file >4 GB into the per-origin Origin Private File System storage path. FROST requires an OPFS file larger than physical RAM so reads bypass the page cache and reach the SSD — legitimate OPFS use rarely exceeds a few hundred MB, so an unexplained multi-GB OPFS allocation is the only host-side tell the Graz paper offers. Rationale: Anchored on the only host-side artefact the article actually names: 'watching your browser's storage for an unexplained multi-gigabyte file is another tell.' The >4 GB threshold mirrors FROST's stated requirement (file > physical RAM to defeat the page cache). Browser-process scope + per-origin OPFS path roots (Chrome/Edge: 'File System/' inside the profile; Firefox: 'storage/default/...fs/'; Safari/WebKit: 'Library/Safari/Storage' or 'Library/WebKit') are taken from the standardised OPFS-on-disk locations referenced by the W3C spec the article cites. No external corroboration searched — there is no actor / malware family / CVE attached, and the IOCs extracted by the pipeline (malicious.app, victim.com, receiver.app, sender.app) are clearly academic placeholders from the paper, not real C2.
ATT&CKT1592.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • In-browser IDEs (StackBlitz WebContainers, VS Code for the Web, Replit, GitPod) which legitimately allocate multi-GB OPFS sandboxes for projects
  • Web-based media editors (Photopea, Figma, CapCut Web) caching large source files
  • Browser-based games persisting asset bundles or save state to OPFS
  • Profile sync / migration tooling temporarily staging the user's browser profile inside the same directory tree
  • Service-worker caches for offline-first PWAs (e.g. mapping apps) that legitimately swell over time
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("stackblitz", "webcontainer", "vscode-web", "replit", "gitpod", "photopea", "figma", "capcut"))
// Add per-tenant: exclude origin folders for sanctioned in-browser IDEs / editors after one pass of investigation
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the origin that owns the OPFS slice (the path component immediately under '/File System/' or '/storage/default/' is the URL-encoded origin). Check the user's recent browser history / open tabs for that origin and whether it is a known-good web IDE / media editor. Pull the parent browser commandline to confirm it's an interactive session and not a headless automation harness. Step 2 — Contain: if the origin is unknown / suspicious, ask the user to close the tab (article notes the measurement only runs while the tab is open) and clear site-data for that origin in browser settings. Snapshot the OPFS file before deletion for forensic review. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the same origin across the fleet — if multiple users have a >4 GB OPFS slice from the same domain, that domain is the indicator, not the file size. Also review whether the same browser session enabled cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP headers) by checking proxy/Zscaler/CSP-report telemetry, since FROST

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","Google Chrome","firefox","Safari","com.apple.WebKit.Networking")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\File System\", "/File System/", "/storage/default/", ".mozilla/firefox", "/Library/Safari/Storage", "/Library/WebKit")
| where FileSize > 4000000000  // 4 GB — FROST requires file > physical RAM

title: Browser writes oversized Origin Private File System (OPFS) file - possible FROST SSD timing side-channel
id: 3f1e9a2c-1d6e-4f0a-9c4f-2b9b5e6a7c01
status: experimental
description: Detects a browser process allocating an unusually large file (>4 GB) inside its per-origin OPFS storage directory. The FROST attack (Graz Univ. of Technology, DIMVA 2026) requires an OPFS file larger than physical RAM so SSD-timing reads bypass the page cache.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-frost-attack-lets-websites-track.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.t1592.004
  - attack.reconnaissance
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '/Google Chrome'
      - '/firefox'
      - '/Safari'
      - '/com.apple.WebKit.Networking'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\File System\'
      - '/File System/'
      - '/storage/default/'
      - '.mozilla/firefox'
      - '/Library/Safari/Storage'
      - '/Library/WebKit'
  selection_size:
    FileSize|gte: 4000000000
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - In-browser IDEs (StackBlitz WebContainers, VS Code Web, Replit, GitPod local) genuinely use multi-GB OPFS
  - Web-based video / photo editors caching large media (Photopea, Figma, CapCut Web)
  - Browser-based game engines persisting save state / asset bundles
level: low
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @EventID:11 (@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\Firefox.exe) OR @process.name:(chrome OR firefox OR Safari OR Google\ Chrome)) (@TargetFilename:(*\File\ System\* OR */File\ System/* OR */storage/default/* OR *.mozilla/firefox/* OR */Library/Safari/Storage/* OR */Library/WebKit/*)) @file.size:>4000000000
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|Safari|WebKit)/i
| regex("(File System|storage/default|\\.mozilla/firefox|Library/Safari/Storage|Library/WebKit)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=[sum(WrittenBytes, as=BytesWritten), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen)])
| BytesWritten > 4000000000
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, max(Filesystem.file_size) as max_size from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","Google Chrome","firefox","Safari","com.apple.WebKit.Networking") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\File System\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/File System/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/storage/default/*/fs/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*.mozilla/firefox/*/storage/default/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/Safari/Storage/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/WebKit/*/Storage/*") AND Filesystem.file_size>4000000000 by host, user, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, max(Filesystem.file_size) as max_size from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","Google Chrome","firefox","Safari","com.apple.WebKit.Networking") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\File System\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/File System/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/storage/default/*/fs/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*.mozilla/firefox/*/storage/default/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/Safari/Storage/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/WebKit/*/Storage/*") AND Filesystem.file_size>4000000000 by host, user, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity

Hades PyPI Attack: 19 Packages Poisoned to Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer

The Hacker News
2026-06-09 15 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Miasma supply chain campaign has sparked a fresh attack wave called Hades, this time involving 37 malicious wheel artifacts across 19 packages in the Python Package Index (PyPI) registry, as the Mini Shai-Hulud-style attacks continue to be refined and splintered to target specific ecosystems. "The compromised releases shipped a *-setup.pth file that attempts to execute automatically

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Hades/Miasma PyPI poisoned package installation (26 named packages) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hades PyPI Attack: 19 Packages Poisoned to Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Python interpreter downloading Bun runtime ZIP from oven-sh GitHub release · [LLM] Hades persistence: *-setup.pth file written into Python site-packages · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Hades C2: GitHub commit search for campaign markers TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime / firedalazer
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Bun runtime reading developer credential files (.npmrc / .pypirc / .ssh / .env / cloud configs) · [LLM] gh-token-monitor service install or rm -rf wiper command (Hades self-destruct) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Hades/Miasma PyPI poisoned package installation (26 named packages) AIDelivery High
Detects pip / python invoking installation of any of the 26 PyPI packages and versions Socket / StepSecurity identified in the Hades wave of the Miasma supply-chain campaign. Catches the very first foothold before the *-setup.pth hook runs on next interpreter start. Rationale: Uses the verbatim 26 package names from the article's two Hades clusters (the 19-package PyPI cluster + the 7-package bioinformatics cluster). Pip-install command line with these exact names is effectively zero-FP outside of incident-response activity.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DFIR / threat-intel analyst intentionally pulling the package into a sandbox for reverse engineering
  • Internal package-mirror sync (e.g. Artifactory / Nexus PyPI proxy) caching the malicious release before takedown
  • Bioinformatics researcher pulling a legitimately-named-but-coincidental fork via an internal index URL
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !contains "sandbox" and FolderPath !has "\\malware_analysis\\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot to DeviceFileEvents on the same host for any *-setup.pth file created after the install and any DeviceNetworkEvents to github.com/oven-sh/bun within 30 min — confirms full chain executed. 2) Contain: isolate host, revoke all developer secrets present (GitHub PAT, npm/PyPI tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure keys, .ssh/*, Anthropic/Claude/MCP configs), force-rotate before reconnecting. 3) Hunt: search the org for any other host that pulled the same package versions in the last 14 days; check internal package mirrors for cached copies; check GitHub org for any repo with description matching 'Hades*The End for the Damned' indicating exfil happened.
let HadesPkgs = dynamic(["bramin","cmd2func","coolbox","dynamo-release","executor-engine","executor-http","funcdesc","magique","magique-ai","mrbios","napari-ufish","nucbox","okite","pantheon-agents","pantheon-toolsets","spateo-release","synago","ufish","uprobe","embiggen","ensmallen","gpsea","mflux-streamlit","nhmpy","ppkt2synergy","pyphetools"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe")
      or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let HadesPkgs = dynamic(["bramin","cmd2func","coolbox","dynamo-release","executor-engine","executor-http","funcdesc","magique","magique-ai","mrbios","napari-ufish","nucbox","okite","pantheon-agents","pantheon-toolsets","spateo-release","synago","ufish","uprobe","embiggen","ensmallen","gpsea","mflux-streamlit","nhmpy","ppkt2synergy","pyphetools"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","python") or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip","python")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "install"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Python interpreter downloading Bun runtime ZIP from oven-sh GitHub release AIInstallation High
Hades/Miasma stages a JavaScript stealer by having the malicious .pth or __init__.py hook download the standalone Bun runtime ZIP from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases. Detecting Python/pip as the parent of that network connection is the cleanest cross-platform pivot — Bun is not a Python dependency in any normal supply chain. Rationale: Article: 'The compromised releases shipped a *-setup.pth file that attempts to execute automatically during Python startup, download the Bun JavaScript runtime, and run an obfuscated JavaScript payload named _index.js.' StepSecurity also notes Bun is downloaded as a standalone ZIP — pivoting on python→github.com/oven-sh/bun is the staging-link signature.
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.007
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually running 'pip install bun-py' or any pip wrapper that legitimately fetches Bun for a project
  • CI job using a Python-based installer/bootstrap (e.g. Ansible play that installs Bun on a dev workstation)
  • Container build step where a Python entrypoint legitimately bootstraps a Bun-based JS toolchain
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun-py","install-bun","@nestjs","bunx"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the parent python's command line — was the install one of the 26 Hades package names? Pull DeviceFileEvents for any .pth or _index.js write between the Python start and the Bun download. 2) Contain: kill the Bun process tree, isolate host, snapshot ~/.bun and any extracted ZIP for forensics, revoke every dev secret the user owns (GitHub PAT, npm token, PyPI token, AWS/GCP/Azure CLI creds, Anthropic/Claude API key). 3) Hunt: look across the org for any other host where python.exe was the parent of a github.com/oven-sh/bun fetch in the last 30 days; check GitHub Actions audit log for the user's PAT scopes being used from unfamiliar runners.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","pip.exe","pip3.exe","bash","sh","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("github.com/oven-sh/bun","objects.githubusercontent.com")
   and (RemoteUrl has_any ("bun-linux","bun-windows","bun-darwin","/releases/download/") or RemoteUrl endswith ".zip")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","pip.exe","pip3.exe")
       or FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","pip.exe","pip3.exe")
    | project DeviceId, PyTimestamp = Timestamp, PyCmd = ProcessCommandLine
) on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (PyTimestamp .. PyTimestamp + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, PyCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let BunUrlFrag = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun","objects.githubusercontent.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Url has_any (BunUrlFrag)
| where Url has_any ("bun-linux","bun-windows","bun-darwin","/releases/download/") or Url endswith ".zip"
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","pip")
    | project DvcHostname, PyTime = TimeGenerated, PyCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
) on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (PyTime .. PyTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, DstHostname, PyCmd
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hades persistence: *-setup.pth file written into Python site-packages AIInstallation High
The Hades cluster persists by dropping a `*-setup.pth` file into a site-packages directory. Python's `site` module executes any `import`/`exec` line in a `.pth` file at every interpreter start, so this file is the auto-run primitive. Detect creation of any file matching the pattern by a non-pip writer or with executable content inside. Rationale: Article: 'the use of a *-setup.pth file that's processed by Python's site module during interpreter startup, resulting in the execution of the malicious payload after installation.' The `-setup.pth` suffix in site-packages is unusual — legitimate .pth files are typically named after the package (e.g. easy-install.pth, distutils-precedence.pth), not '<pkg>-setup.pth'.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom internal setup.py / build backends that author a vendor-named '*-setup.pth' (rare but possible)
  • DFIR analyst restoring a sample for reversing into an isolated venv
  • Editable-install ('pip install -e') artefact named *-setup.pth from an unusual build tool
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--editable"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the .pth contents (Defender 'Run query' / live response → small file, plain text). Genuine .pth files are single import lines; Hades .pth contains exec() / urllib code downloading Bun. 2) Contain: delete the .pth (it executes on every python start including services), isolate host, kill any running bun / _index.js processes, revoke developer secrets owned by AccountName. 3) Hunt: search every Python venv/system site-packages on the host and across the fleet for the same filename pattern; check whether the same SHA256 appears anywhere else; pivot to the parent pip install command and check whether it shows up on any other host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith "-setup.pth"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\site-packages\", "/site-packages/", @"\dist-packages\", "/dist-packages/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName endswith "-setup.pth"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\site-packages\", "/site-packages/", @"\dist-packages\", "/dist-packages/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime reading developer credential files (.npmrc / .pypirc / .ssh / .env / cloud configs) AIActions on Objectives High
The Hades JavaScript stealer (_index.js) executes inside Bun and walks the developer's home directory for credentials: .npmrc, .pypirc, .env, .aws/credentials, .config/gcloud, .azure, .docker, ~/.ssh/, ~/.config/Claude, MCP configs, Vault tokens, shell histories. Bun touching those paths is the credential_access signature. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact target set: 'secrets associated with GitHub, npm, PyPI, RubyGems, JFrog, CircleCI, Anthropic, AWS, GCP, Azure, and Kubernetes, along with Docker configurations, Vault tokens, SSH keys, shell histories, .env files, .npmrc files, .pypirc files, Claude/MCP configurations.' Bun as the reader is what makes this fire — legitimate dev tools (git, gh, aws-cli) reading these is normal; Bun reading 3+ distinct credential paths in one session is not.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Bun-based dev tool (e.g. wrangler, supabase, drizzle) that legitimately reads .env for project config
  • Bun-based deployment script that reads .aws/credentials to deploy infra
  • Engineer running 'bun test' in a repo whose test setup reads ~/.npmrc
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wrangler","supabase","drizzle","vite","next","astro") and SecretReads < 5)
Response runbook
1) Triage: list every path Bun touched in the window (group by FolderPath); a 'real' Bun app reads ~/.env in its own project dir, malware fans out to .ssh, .aws AND .npmrc AND Claude AND .docker. Read the parent process — was Python the grandparent? Was a *-setup.pth file run? 2) Contain: kill all bun processes, isolate host, mass-revoke every secret in the read set (GitHub PATs, npm/PyPI tokens, AWS access keys, GCP service-account keys, Anthropic API keys, all SSH keys), force-rotate before reissue. 3) Hunt: pivot to GitHub audit log for unfamiliar PAT use; check the user's GitHub repos for new repos whose description matches 'Hades*The End for the Damned' (the campaign exfil marker); check whether the same Bun SHA256 has run on any other host.
let SecretPaths = pack_array(".npmrc",".pypirc",".env","credentials","id_rsa","id_ed25519","gcloud",".azure","config.json","mcp.json",".vault-token",".bash_history",".zsh_history","gh-token",".jfrog",".gem");
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileModified")
   and (FolderPath has_any (@"\.ssh\", "/.ssh/", @"\.aws\", "/.aws/", @"\.azure\", "/.azure/", @"\gcloud\", "/gcloud/", @"\.docker\", "/.docker/", @"\Claude\", "/Claude/", @"\.config\Claude\", @"\.jfrog\", "/.jfrog/")
        or FileName in~ (".npmrc",".pypirc",".env","credentials",".vault-token",".bash_history",".zsh_history","mcp.json")
        or FileName startswith "id_")
| summarize SecretReads = dcount(FolderPath), Paths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where SecretReads >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileOpened","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/", @"\.ssh\", "/.aws/", @"\.aws\", "/.azure/", @"\.azure\", "/gcloud/", "/.docker/", "/Claude/", "/.jfrog/")
    or TargetFileName in~ (".npmrc",".pypirc",".env","credentials",".vault-token",".bash_history",".zsh_history","mcp.json")
    or TargetFileName startswith "id_"
| summarize SecretReads = dcount(TargetFilePath), Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where SecretReads >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\bun.exe OR *\bun) OR @process.executable.path:(*/bun OR */bun.exe)) AND (@TargetFilename:(*\.npmrc OR *\.pypirc OR *\.env OR *\.aws\credentials OR *\.ssh\id_* OR *\.azure\* OR *\.docker\config.json OR *\Claude\* OR *mcp.json OR *\.vault-token OR *\.jfrog\*) OR @file.path:(*/.npmrc OR */.pypirc OR */.env OR */.aws/credentials OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.azure/* OR */.docker/config.json OR */Claude/* OR */mcp.json OR */.vault-token OR */.jfrog/*))

gh-token-monitor service install or rm -rf wiper command (Hades self-destruct) AIActions on Objectives High
Hades installs a background service named 'gh-token-monitor' that doubles as a wiper — if the developer revokes the stolen GitHub token, the service triggers `rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents`. Either the service-install or the wiper command is article-specific and warrants an alert. Rationale: Article: 'Install a background service named gh-token-monitor that acts as a wiper by removing all data (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents) if the stolen GitHub token is revoked by the developer.' The service name and the exact wiper command line are both unique enough to alert directly on string match.
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1543.002 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Services
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team / purple-team replicating the Hades chain in a lab
  • Security researcher detonating the malware in a controlled VM with EDR shipping to prod tenant
  • Sysadmin's deliberate cleanup script that happens to chain rm -rf ~ with rm -rf ~/Documents (highly unusual)
Response runbook
1) Triage: this is a CRITICAL — wiper attempts may already be running. Immediately check whether the rm -rf process completed and how much was destroyed (DeviceFileEvents on FileDeleted for the same DeviceId, last 5 min). 2) Contain: isolate host instantly (Defender Live Response 'isolate'), kill the gh-token-monitor service before it triggers, snapshot the disk for forensics, restore from backup if data is gone. 3) Hunt: search the whole fleet for the same service name and the same rm -rf command pattern in last 30 days; check GitHub audit log for the dev's PAT being used from unfamiliar runners (the wiper trigger is PAT revocation, so revocation may be in flight); search GitHub for any new repo by the user described 'Hades*The End for the Damned' indicating exfil completed before the wiper armed.
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "gh-token-monitor"
     and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sc create","sc.exe create","systemctl","launchctl","New-Service","systemd")
  | extend Pivot = "service_install"
),
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~/?|/home/[^/\s]+/?|/Users/[^/\s]+/?)\s*;\s*rm\s+-rf\s+~?/?Documents"
  | extend Pivot = "wiper"
),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
  | where AdditionalFields has "gh-token-monitor" or FileName has "gh-token-monitor" or ProcessCommandLine has "gh-token-monitor"
  | extend Pivot = "service_event"
)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Pivot, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "gh-token-monitor"
     and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sc create","sc.exe create","systemctl","launchctl","New-Service")
  | extend Pivot = "service_install"
),
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~/?|/home/[^/\s]+/?|/Users/[^/\s]+/?)\s*;\s*rm\s+-rf\s+~?/?Documents"
  | extend Pivot = "wiper"
),
( SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 7045
  | where ServiceName has "gh-token-monitor" or ServiceFileName has "gh-token-monitor"
  | extend Pivot = "service_event", ActingProcessCommandLine = ServiceFileName, DvcHostname = Computer, ActorUsername = SubjectUserName
)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Pivot, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
